prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1448; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a vehicle entering from the cross street. Claimant reports being the driver of the struck vehicle. Claimant states head struck the window frame on impact and reports ongoing headache and dizziness. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Advised claimant of the claims process and requested the police report number.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant confirmed the other driver admitted running the amber light, though this is not yet documented in the police report. Claimant describes pain at the back of the head and difficulty concentrating at work. Claimant has not yet seen a physician for the head injury. Recommended medical evaluation and explained that medical records will be needed to support the injury portion of the claim.

Entry 3: Received photos of both vehicles from claimant. Driver door and rear quarter panel show deep intrusion consistent with a side impact. Airbag deployed on the claimant's side. Scene diagram from police report reviewed and matches the claimant's account of the direction of travel. Recorded that claimant has no attorney and has not signed any release.

Entry 4: Claimant reports they were seen at an urgent care facility and diagnosed with a concussion. Requested the discharge paperwork and any follow-up referral. Claimant indicates symptoms include light sensitivity and short-term memory lapses. Advised claimant that a neurology or primary care follow-up is typically needed and that wage loss documentation should be gathered if time off work is taken.

Entry 5: Liability position under review. Police report and other driver's statement indicate a possible conflict on signal phase, so fault allocation is not yet final. Claimant was informed of the current status and that a decision on the injury evaluation will follow receipt of complete medical records. Diary set for follow-up with claimant in two weeks.
